# Market Update: Stocks vs Bonds Checkup

Report 147 | Published 2024-10-13 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2024-10-13/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/147.json)

Treasury demand, bitcoin financing, and valuation dispersion.

Strongest concrete results were bitcoin breakout and rapid corporate accumulation. The bank-financing discussion has useful balance-sheet intuition but bank purchases are not identical to central-bank QE. Relative valuation and stocks-versus-bonds preferences lack fixed horizons; dividend growth should be distinguished from investor returns.

**Coverage:** All macro, digital-asset, stock/bond and gold/dollar sections read. Historical 2019 bond performance assertions are repeats; not new forecasts. No portfolio trades reconstructed.

### 147-C12

**Premium shorting can fail.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | mstr-short-convergence-risk |
| Source blocks | 49, 50, 61 |
| Thesis family | mstr-short-convergence-risk |

An overpriced asset can appreciate before converging; no finite bound on losses follows from NAV premium alone. This does not establish a particular fund failure.

**Direction:** Supported for the defined proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Deductive assessment:**

- One share shorted at P0
- No binding future price cap
- Ignore borrow fees, which only worsen losses

Short profit=P 0-Pt. NAV premium alone imposes no bound on Pt, so losses need not wait for or end with convergence.

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.
